speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for National Development whether the Ministry will develop an action plan for urban wildlife management in consultation with nature groups and with a stronger focus on co-existence measures rather than removal of wildlife which reinforces the mindset that native wildlife are pests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This is one of the key thrusts of NParks’ wildlife management approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, NParks partners these stakeholders to develop educational resources and outreach initiatives to advise the community on how to respond to wildlife sightings and to raise public awareness on the negative impact of feeding wildlife.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In addition, NParks works with stakeholders to host its monthly human-wildlife encounters webinar series, to promote responsible behaviour during such encounters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, by identifying wildlife hotspots, NParks is able to implement mitigation measures against roadkill, such as putting in place vehicle speed reduction measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: All of us can also play our part by not feeding wildlife, keeping our residential areas clean and appreciating wildlife from a safe distance.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I ask specifically whether we can stop the poisoning of wild animals?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The problem here is that it is not just the target species that dies but there is a huge knock-on effect.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Just recently, ACRES rescued a white-bellied sea eagle which had consumed a poisoned wildlife.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Thankfully, it recovered and was released back into the wild but there were many cases where cats, dogs, other animals consume the poisoned animal and they subsequently die.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, could I ask whether we can stop this practice – not have measures in place during the poisoning exercise but stop this practice altogether?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Our approach towards wildlife management, as I have mentioned, is such that we would have to be very much based on the science of animal management.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We would need to study the ecology and, where possible, to work on the upstream measures.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The upstream measures are very key and include food source reduction.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, this is where we place a lot of our efforts.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Where necessary, we would also consider animal control measures, but these would have to be done in a humane and safe manner.
